questions.question_text: Which one of the following keep tracks of the execution of the program?
questions.answer: The program counter holds the address of the next instruction to be executed, thereby tracking program execution.

questions.question_text: When an instruction depends on the result of previous instruction that hazard is termed as
questions.answer: A data hazard occurs when an instruction needs an operand that a preceding instruction has not yet produced.

questions.question_text: In pipelining concept, to increase the speed of the memory access, we use
questions.answer: Cache is a fast memory that supplies instructions/data in about one clock cycle so pipeline stages are not stalled.

questions.question_text: The first machine cycle of an instruction is always a
questions.answer: Every instruction begins with the opcode fetch cycle.

questions.question_text: Time lost as a result of branch instruction is called
questions.answer: Branch penalty is the number of cycles wasted (stalls/flushed instructions) due to a branch.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT considered as software Parallelism
questions.answer: Memory parallelism is a hardware-level form of parallelism (e.g. interleaved memory); task-level, data and transaction-level parallelism are software parallelism.
MISD — in Flynn's classification pipelined processors are usually cited as MISD, since several stages each perform a different operation on the same data stream.

questions.question_text: When the processor is executing in Jazelle state, ... [rest of the question and options cut off in the source image; only option a) 32 is visible]
questions.answer: In Jazelle state the ARM processor executes 8-bit Java bytecode instructions (ARM state = 32-bit, Thumb state = 16-bit instructions).
